subject: Civil Engineering
title: Stormwater Drainage Systems
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Stormwater Drainage Systems.

hook.text: A city without storm drains floods in any heavy rain. Underground pipes save streets.

buildup.text: Catch basins grab runoff from gutters. Pipes slope downhill to outfall points in rivers.

discovery.text: The rational method sizes storm pipes — peak flow equals rainfall times area times runoff.

twist.text: Combined sewers carry both stormwater and sewage — heavy rain overwhelms treatment plants.

climax.text: Chicago reversed its river flow in 1900 to keep sewage out of Lake Michigan — a mega-project.

punchline.text: Below every dry street is a river of stormwater flowing out of sight.

quiz.question: What problem occurs when combined sewers overflow during heavy rain?
options: Storm drains become blocked with debris
Untreated sewage and stormwater discharge directly into waterways
The treatment plant produces excess clean water
